title.zh: 卷五十三 列傳第二十三 愍懷太子
title.raw: 卷五十三 列傳第二十三 愍懷太子 Volume 53 Biographies 23: Crown Prince Minhuai

units.zh: 愍懷太子
units.literal: Crown Prince Minhuai
units.idiomatic: Crown Prince Minhuai

units.zh: 湣懷太子遹，字熙祖，惠帝長子，母曰謝才人。
units.literal: Crown Prince Minhuai, Yu, courtesy name Xizu, was Emperor Hui's eldest son; his mother was Talented Lady Xie.
units.idiomatic: Crown Prince Minhuai, Yu, courtesy name Xizu, was Emperor Hui's eldest son; his mother was Talented Lady Xie.

units.zh: 幼而聰慧，武帝愛之，恆在左右。
units.literal: From childhood he was clever and bright; Emperor Wu loved him and kept him always at his side.
units.idiomatic: From childhood he was clever and bright; Emperor Wu loved him and kept him always at his side.

units.zh: 初，賈后母郭槐欲以韓壽女為太子妃，太子亦欲婚韓氏以自固。
units.literal: Earlier Empress Jia's mother Guo Huai had wished to take Han Shou's daughter as crown princess; the crown prince also wished to marry the Hans to strengthen himself.
units.idiomatic: Earlier, Empress Jia's mother, Guo Huai, had wanted Han Shou's daughter to become crown princess. The crown prince also hoped that marrying into the Han family would strengthen his position.

units.zh: 而壽妻賈午及後皆不聽，而為太子聘王衍小女惠風。
units.literal: But Han Shou's wife Jia Wu and the empress both refused and instead betrothed the crown prince to Wang Yan's younger daughter Huifeng.
units.idiomatic: But Han Shou's wife Jia Wu and the empress both refused, and instead betrothed the crown prince to Wang Yan's younger daughter Huifeng.

units.zh: 太子聞衍長女美，而賈后為謐聘之，心不能平，頗以為言。
units.literal: The crown prince heard Wang's elder daughter was beautiful while the empress betrothed her to Jia Mi; his heart could not rest easy and he spoke of it often.
units.idiomatic: The crown prince heard Wang's elder daughter was beautiful while the empress betrothed her to Jia Mi; his heart could not rest easy and he spoke of it often.

units.zh: 謐嘗與太子圍棋，爭道，成都王穎見而訶謐，謐意愈不平，因此譖太子于後曰：「太子廣買田業，多畜私財以結小人者，為賈氏故也。
units.literal: Once Mi played go with the crown prince and they quarreled over the move; Ying, Prince of Chengdu, saw and rebuked Mi; Mi grew more resentful and therefore slandered the crown prince to the empress: 'The crown prince buys fields wholesale, hoards private wealth, and courts petty men—all because of the Jia clan.
units.idiomatic: Once while playing go with the crown prince Mi quarreled over a move; Ying, Prince of Chengdu, saw and rebuked Mi; Mi grew more resentful and slandered the crown prince to the empress: "The crown prince buys fields wholesale, hoards private wealth, and courts petty men—all because of the Jia clan.

units.zh: 沙門，太子小字也。
units.literal: 'Shamen' was the crown prince's childhood byname.
units.idiomatic: 'Shamen' was the crown prince's childhood byname.

units.zh: 初，太子之廢也，妃父王衍表請離婚。
units.literal: When the crown prince was first deposed, his father-in-law Wang Yan memorialized requesting divorce.
units.idiomatic: When the crown prince was first deposed, his father-in-law Wang Yan memorialized requesting divorce.

units.zh: 太子至許，遺妃書曰：「鄙雖頑愚，心念為善，欲盡忠孝之節，無有惡逆之心。
units.literal: After the crown prince reached Xu he sent his consort a letter: 'Though I am coarse and foolish at heart I wished to do good and fulfill loyalty and filial piety—I harbored no rebellious evil.
units.idiomatic: After reaching Xu he sent his consort a letter: "Though I am coarse and foolish, at heart I wished to do good and fulfill loyalty and filial piety—I harbored no rebellious evil.

label.en: Right Vice Director of the Secretariat

title.zh: 卷七十七 晉書3: 高祖本紀三
title.en: Volume 77 Book of Later Jin 3: Gaozu Annals 3
title.raw: 卷七十七 晉書3: 高祖本紀三 Volume 77 Book of Later Jin 3: Gaozu Annals 3

units.zh: 天福三年正月戊申朔，帝御崇元殿受朝賀，仗衛如式。
units.literal: In the third year of Tianfu, first month, on the first day of the month (wushen), the Emperor took the throne in Chongyuan Hall to receive court congratulations; guards and escorts followed the prescribed form.
units.idiomatic: On the first day of the first month of Tianfu 3, the emperor entered Chongyuan Hall to receive the New Year court congratulations, with guards and ceremonial escorts in full order.

units.zh: 己酉，百官守司，以太史先奏日蝕故也。
units.literal: On jiyou, the hundred officials kept their posts, because the Grand Astrologer had beforehand reported a solar eclipse.
units.idiomatic: On jiyou the officials remained at their posts, since the court astrologer had already forecast an eclipse of the sun.

units.zh: 至是不虧，內外稱賀。
units.literal: When it came to this, there was no eclipse; inside and outside offered congratulations.
units.idiomatic: When the moment came, the sun was not dimmed, and court and capital alike offered congratulations.

units.zh: 七月丙午朔，差左諫議大夫薛融、秘書監呂琦、駕部員外郎兼侍御史知雜事劉皞、刑部郎中司徒詡、大理正張仁彖，同共詳定唐明宗朝編敕。
units.literal: In the seventh month, on the first day (bingwu), Xue Rong, Left Remonstrance Counselor; Lü Qi, Director of the Palace Library; Liu Hao, Director of the Transport Office and concurrent Supervising Censor with charge of mixed affairs; Situ Xu, Director of the Ministry of Punishments; and Zhang Rentuan, Senior Rectifier of the Court of Judicial Review, were jointly dispatched to examine and fix the compiled edicts of the Tang reign of Emperor Mingzong.
units.idiomatic: On bingwu, the first day of the seventh month, Xue Rong, Left Remonstrance Counselor; Lü Qi, Director of the Palace Library; Liu Hao, Transport Office Vice Director and concurrent Supervising Censor in charge of miscellaneous affairs; Situ Xu, Director in the Ministry of Punishments; and Zhang Rentuan, Senior Rectifier of the Court of Judicial Review, were jointly assigned to review and revise the compiled edicts of the Tang reign of Emperor Mingzong.

units.zh: 庚戌，御史中丞王延改尚書右丞，尚書右丞盧導改尚書吏部侍郎，以左諫議大夫薛融為御史中丞。
units.literal: On gengxu, Censor-in-Chief Wang Yan was changed to Right Vice Director of the Secretariat; Right Vice Director Lu Dao was changed to Vice Minister of Personnel; Left Remonstrance Counselor Xue Rong was appointed Censor-in-Chief.
units.idiomatic: On gengxu Wang Yan moved from censor-in-chief to right vice director of the Secretariat; Lu Dao from right vice director to vice minister of personnel; and Xue Rong from left remonstrance counselor to censor-in-chief.

units.zh: 辛酉，制皇帝受命寶，以「受天明命，惟德允昌」為文。
units.literal: On xinyou, the Imperial Seal of Received Mandate was cast, with the inscription "Receiving Heaven's clear mandate, virtue alone brings prosperity."
units.idiomatic: On xinyou the imperial Seal of Received Mandate was cast, inscribed "Receiving Heaven's clear mandate—only virtue brings lasting prosperity."

title.en: Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices

title.zh: 卷八十三 晉書9: 少帝本紀三
title.en: Volume 83 Book of Later Jin 9: Emperor Shao 3
title.raw: 卷八十三 晉書9: 少帝本紀三 Volume 83 Book of Later Jin 9: Emperor Shao 3

units.zh: 開運元年秋七月辛未朔，帝御崇元殿，大赦天下，改天福九年為開運元年。
units.literal: On the first day of the seventh month of autumn in the first year of Kaiyun, xinwei, the Emperor took the throne at Chongyuan Hall, proclaimed a general amnesty throughout the realm, and changed the ninth year of Tianfu to the first year of Kaiyun.
units.idiomatic: On the first day of the seventh month in autumn of Kaiyun 1, xinwei, the Emperor held court in Chongyuan Hall, granted a general amnesty, and renamed the ninth year of Tianfu as the first year of Kaiyun.

units.zh: 河北諸州，曾經契丹蹂踐處，與免今年秋稅。
units.literal: In all prefectures of Hebei that had suffered Khitan ravaging and trampling, the autumn tax of this year was remitted.
units.idiomatic: All prefectures in Hebei that had been ravaged by the Khitan were granted exemption from this year's autumn tax.

units.zh: 諸軍將士等第各賜優給。
units.literal: Officers and soldiers of the various armies were each granted generous rewards according to rank.
units.idiomatic: Soldiers and officers in the various armies received graded bonuses according to merit.

units.zh: 北京留守劉知遠充北面行營都統，鎮州節度使杜威充北面行營都招討使，鄆州節度使張從恩充馬步軍都監，西京留守景延廣充馬步軍都排陣使，徐州節度使趙在禮充馬步軍都虞候，晉州節度使安叔千充馬步軍左廂排陣使，前兗州節度使安審信充馬軍右廂排陣使，河中節度使安審琦充馬步軍都指揮使，河陽節度使符彥卿充馬軍左廂都指揮使，滑州節度使皇甫遇充馬步軍右廂都指揮使，右神武統軍張彥澤充馬軍排陣使，滄州節度使王廷胤充馬軍左廂都指揮使，陜州節度使宋彥筠充步軍右廂都指揮使，前金州節度使田武充步軍左廂排陣使，左神武統軍潘環充步軍右廂排陣使。
units.literal: Liu Zhiyuan, military commissioner of the Northern Capital, was made overall commander of the northern campaign headquarters; Du Wei, military governor of Zhenzhou, was made overall commander for suppression; Zhang Cong'en, military governor of Yanzhou, was made overall supervisor of horse and foot armies; Jing Yanguang, military commissioner of the Western Capital, was made overall array marshal of horse and foot armies; Zhao Zaili, military governor of Xuzhou, was made overall deputy commander of horse and foot armies; An Shuqian, military governor of Jinzhou, was made array marshal of the left wing of horse and foot armies; An Shenxin, former military governor of Yanzhou, was made array marshal of the right wing of the cavalry; An Shenqi, military governor of Hezhong, was made overall commander of horse and foot armies; Fu Yanqing, military governor of Heyang, was made overall commander of the left wing of cavalry; Huangfu Yu, military governor of Huazhou, was made overall commander of the right wing of horse and foot armies; Zhang Yanzhe, Commander of the Right Divine Martial Army, was made cavalry array marshal; Wang Tingyin, military governor of Cangzhou, was made overall commander of the left wing of cavalry; Song Yanyun, military governor of Shaanzhou, was made overall commander of the right wing of infantry; Tian Wu, former military governor of Jinzhou, was made array marshal of the left wing of infantry; Pan Huan, Commander of the Left Divine Martial Army, was made array marshal of the right wing of infantry.
units.idiomatic: Liu Zhiyuan, military commissioner of the Northern Capital, became overall commander of the northern campaign; Du Wei of Zhenzhou, overall commander for suppression; Zhang Cong'en of Yanzhou, overall supervisor of horse and foot; Jing Yanguang, military commissioner of the Western Capital, overall array marshal; Zhao Zaili of Xuzhou, overall deputy commander; An Shuqian of Jinzhou, left-wing array marshal; former Yanzhou governor An Shenxin, right-wing cavalry array marshal; An Shenqi of Hezhong, overall commander of horse and foot; Fu Yanqing of Heyang, left-wing cavalry commander; Huangfu Yu of Huazhou, right-wing horse-and-foot commander; Zhang Yanzhe of the Right Divine Martial Army, cavalry array marshal; Wang Tingyin of Cangzhou, left-wing cavalry commander; Song Yanyun of Shaanzhou, right-wing infantry commander; former Jinzhou governor Tian Wu, left-wing infantry array marshal; and Pan Huan of the Left Divine Martial Army, right-wing infantry array marshal.

units.zh: 壬寅，閩王王延羲為其下連重遇、朱文進所害，眾推文進知留後事，稱天福年號，間道以聞。
units.literal: On renyin, the King of Min Wang Yanxi was killed by his subordinates Lian Chongyu and Zhu Wenjin; the multitude pushed Zhu Wenjin to manage the affairs of military commissioner, adopted the Tianfu era name, and reported by a secret route.
units.idiomatic: On renyin, King Yanxi of Min was murdered by his officers Lian Chongyu and Zhu Wenjin; the troops installed Zhu Wenjin as acting military commissioner, proclaimed the Tianfu era name, and sent word by a back channel.

units.zh: 甲辰，太子少傅盧文紀改太子太傅，太子少保李麟改太子太保，刑部尚書李懌改戶部尚書，給事中司徒詡改右散騎常侍，以府州刺史折從阮為安北都護，充振武節度使。
units.literal: On jiachen, Lu Wenji, Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, was transferred to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent; Li Lin, Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, was transferred to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent; Li Yi, Minister of Justice, was transferred to Minister of Revenue; Situ Xu, Attendant Censor, was transferred to Right Regular Attendant of the Cavalry; She Congruan, prefect of Fu Prefecture, was made Protector-General Pacifying the North and appointed military governor of Zhenwu.
units.idiomatic: On jiachen, Lu Wenji rose from Junior to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent; Li Lin from Junior to Grand Guardian; Li Yi moved from Justice to Revenue; Situ Xu from Attendant Censor to Right Regular Attendant of the Cavalry; and She Congruan, prefect of Fu, was named Protector-General Pacifying the North and military governor of Zhenwu.

units.zh: 丙戌，降青州為防禦使額，以萊州刺史楊承勛為汝州防禦使。
units.literal: On bingxu, Qingzhou was reduced to a defense commission, and Yang Chengxun, prefect of Laizhou, was made defense commissioner of Ruzhou.
units.idiomatic: On bingxu, Qingzhou was downgraded to a defense command, and Yang Chengxun, prefect of Laizhou, was appointed defense commissioner of Ruzhou.

units.zh: 己丑，以工部尚書竇貞固為禮部尚書，太常卿王延為工部尚書，左丞王松為太常卿，以前尚書右丞龍敏為尚書左丞。
units.literal: On jichou, Dou Zhengu, Minister of Works, was made Minister of Rites; Wang Yan, Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, was made Minister of Works; Wang Song, Left Assistant Director, was made Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; Long Min, former Right Assistant Director, was made Left Assistant Director.
units.idiomatic: On jichou, Dou Zhengu moved from Works to Rites; Wang Yan from Director of Sacrifices to Works; Wang Song from Left Assistant Director to Director of Sacrifices; and former Right Assistant Director Long Min to Left Assistant Director.

units.zh: 癸巳，以前安州防禦使李建崇為河陽兵馬留後，以宣徽使翟光鄴為青州防禦使，以內客省使李彥韜為宣徽北院使。
units.literal: On guisi, Li Jianchong, former defense commissioner of Anzhou, was made military regent of Heyang; Zhai Guangye, Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat, was made defense commissioner of Qingzhou; Li Yantao, Commissioner of the Inner Clients Bureau, was made Commissioner of the North Court of the Palace Secretariat.
units.idiomatic: On guisi, Li Jianchong, former defense commissioner of Anzhou, became military regent of Heyang; Zhai Guangye, Palace Secretariat commissioner, defense commissioner of Qingzhou; and Li Yantao, commissioner of the Inner Clients Bureau, commissioner of the North Court of the Palace Secretariat.

units.zh: 資治通鑑 第131卷
units.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 131
units.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 131

units.zh: 【宋紀十三】　柔兆敦牂，一年。
units.literal: [Song Records 13] Rouzhao Dunzang; one year in all.
units.idiomatic: [Song Records 13] Rouzhao Dunzang—one year in all.

units.zh: 太宗明皇帝上之下泰始二年（
units.literal: The lower portion of the upper fascicle on Emperor Ming the Brilliant: Taishi year 2 (
units.idiomatic: Emperor Ming the Brilliant, upper fascicle, lower portion—Taishi year 2 (

units.zh: 會稽人大懼，將士多奔亡，孔凱不能制。
units.literal: The people of Kuaiji were greatly afraid; officers and soldiers mostly fled; Kong Kai could not control them.
units.idiomatic: The people of Kuaiji were terrified; officers and soldiers fled in droves; Kong Kai could not control them.

units.zh: 戊寅，上虞令王晏起兵攻郡，凱逃奔脊山；
units.literal: On wuyin, Shangyu magistrate Wang Yan raised troops to attack the commandery; Kai fled to Jishan;
units.idiomatic: On wuyin, Shangyu magistrate Wang Yan raised troops against the commandery; Kong Kai fled to Jishan;

units.zh: 車騎從事中郎張綏封府庫以待吳喜。
units.literal: Chief Clerk to the General of Chariots and Cavalry Zhang Sui sealed the government treasury to await Wu Xi.
units.idiomatic: Chief clerk to the general of chariots and cavalry Zhang Sui sealed the government treasury to await Wu Xi.

units.zh: 己卯，王晏入城，殺綏，執尋陽王子房於別署。
units.literal: On jimao, Wang Yan entered the city, killed Sui, and seized Prince of Xunyang Zifang at a separate residence.
units.idiomatic: On jimao, Wang Yan entered the city, killed Zhang Sui, and seized Prince of Xunyang Liu Zifang at a separate residence.

units.zh: 縱兵大掠，府庫皆空；
units.literal: He let the troops plunder freely; the treasury was emptied;
units.idiomatic: He let his troops plunder freely; the treasury was emptied;

units.zh: 獲孔璪，殺之。
units.literal: they captured Kong Zuan and killed him.
units.idiomatic: they captured Kong Zuan and killed him.

units.zh: 庚辰，脊山民縛孔凱送晏，晏謂之曰：「此事孔璪所為，無預卿事，可作首辭，當相為申上。」
units.literal: On gengchen, the people of Jishan bound Kong Kai and sent him to Yan; Yan said to him: "This affair was Kong Zuan's doing; it does not involve you; you may compose a memorial of confession and I shall present it on your behalf to the throne."
units.idiomatic: On gengchen, the people of Jishan bound Kong Kai and sent him to Wang Yan; Yan said to him: "This was Kong Zuan's doing and does not involve you; draft a confession and I will present it for you at court."

units.zh: 凱曰：「江東處分，莫不由身；
units.literal: Kai said: "Every disposition in Jiangdong was none other than my own;
units.idiomatic: Kong Kai said: "Every decision in the Jiangdong region was mine alone;

units.zh: 委罪求活，便是君輩行意耳。」
units.literal: to shift blame to seek life—that is precisely your sort's intent."
units.idiomatic: to shift blame to save my skin—that is exactly your sort's way."

units.zh: 晏乃斬之。
units.literal: Yan then beheaded him.
units.idiomatic: Yan then beheaded him.

units.zh: 顧琛、王曇生、袁標等詣吳喜歸罪，喜皆宥之。
units.literal: Gu Chen, Wang Tansheng, Yuan Biao, and others came to Wu Xi to surrender blame; Xi pardoned them all.
units.idiomatic: Gu Chen, Wang Tansheng, Yuan Biao, and others came to Wu Xi to surrender; Xi pardoned them all.

record.descriptor: Former Qin Administrator of Zhongshan, Inspector of Pingzhou

value.statement: Killed by Murong Lin when Boling fell.

title.zh: 卷一百一十五 載記第十五 苻丕 苻登
title.en: Volume 115 Records 15: Fu Pi; Fu Deng
title.raw: 卷一百一十五 載記第十五 苻丕 苻登 Volume 115 Records 15: Fu Pi; Fu Deng

units.zh: 苻丕 苻登
units.literal: Fu Pi; Fu Deng.
units.idiomatic: This chapter records Fu Pi and Fu Deng.

units.zh: 苻丕，字永叔，堅之長庶子也。
units.literal: Fu Pi, style name Yongshu, was Fu Jian's eldest son by a concubine.
units.idiomatic: Fu Pi, whose courtesy name was Yongshu, was Fu Jian's eldest son born to a secondary consort.

units.zh: 少而聰彗好學，博綜經史。
units.literal: From youth he was clever and fond of learning, and broadly versed in the classics and histories.
units.idiomatic: Even as a boy he showed quick intelligence and a love of books, with wide learning in classical texts and historical works.

units.zh: 堅尚書令、魏昌公苻纂自關中來奔，拜太尉，進封東海王。
units.literal: Fu Jian's Director of the Secretariat and Duke of Weichang Fu Zuan came fleeing from Guanzhong and was appointed Grand Commandant, advanced to Prince of Donghai.
units.idiomatic: Fu Zuan, Fu Jian's director of the secretariat and duke of Weichang, arrived as a refugee from Guanzhong; Fu Pi named him grand commandant and raised him to prince of Donghai.

units.zh: 以中山太守王兗為平東將軍、平州刺史、阜城侯，苻定為征東將軍、冀州牧、高城侯，苻紹為鎮東將軍、督冀州諸軍事、重合侯，苻謨為征西將軍、幽州牧、高邑侯，苻亮為鎮北大將軍、督幽、并二州諸軍事，並進爵郡公。
units.literal: He made the Administrator of Zhongshan Wang Yan General Who Pacifies the East, Inspector of Pingzhou, and Marquis of Fucheng; Fu Ding General Who Conquers the East, Governor of Jizhou, and Marquis of Gaocheng; Fu Shao General Who Guards the East, Supervisor of Military Affairs in Jizhou, and Marquis of Chonghe; Fu Mo General Who Conquers the West, Governor of Youzhou, and Marquis of Gaoyi; Fu Liang General Who Guards the North, Commander of Military Affairs in You and Bing, and all were advanced in noble rank to Dukes of commanderies.
units.idiomatic: Wang Yan of Zhongshan became general who pacifies the east, inspector of Pingzhou, and marquis of Fucheng; Fu Ding general who conquers the east, governor of Jizhou, and marquis of Gaocheng; Fu Shao general who guards the east, with overall command in Jizhou, and marquis of Chonghe; Fu Mo general who conquers the west, governor of Youzhou, and marquis of Gaoyi; Fu Liang general who guards the north, with joint authority over You and Bing—all were promoted to commandery dukes.

units.zh: 定、紹據信都，謨、亮先據常山，慕容垂之圍鄴城也，並降于垂，聞丕稱尊號，遣使謝罪。
units.literal: Ding and Shao held Xindu; Mo and Liang had first occupied Changshan; when Murong Chui besieged Ye they had both surrendered to Chui, but on hearing that Fu Pi had assumed the imperial title they sent envoys to apologize.
units.idiomatic: Fu Ding and Fu Shao held Xindu while Fu Mo and Fu Liang had seized Changshan first; both pairs had gone over to Murong Chui when he invested Ye, yet when Fu Pi declared himself emperor they dispatched messengers begging forgiveness.

units.zh: 王兗固守博陵，與垂相持。
units.literal: Wang Yan stubbornly defended Boling against Chui.
units.idiomatic: Wang Yan shut himself in Boling and held the line against Murong Chui.

units.zh: 左將軍竇沖、秦州刺史王統、河州刺史毛興、益州刺史王廣、南秦州刺史楊璧、衛將軍楊定，並據隴右，遣使招丕，請討姚萇。
units.literal: The General of the Left Dou Chong, the Inspector of Qinzhou Wang Tong, the Inspector of Hezhou Mao Xing, the Inspector of Yizhou Wang Guang, the Inspector of South Qinzhou Yang Bi, and the General of the Guards Yang Ding all held Longyou and sent envoys to summon Fu Pi, asking to campaign against Yao Chang.
units.idiomatic: Dou Chong, general of the left; Wang Tong, inspector of Qinzhou; Mao Xing, inspector of Hezhou; Wang Guang, inspector of Yizhou; Yang Bi, inspector of south Qinzhou; and Yang Ding, general of the guards, each held ground in Longyou and wrote to Fu Pi offering to strike Yao Chang.

units.zh: 君臣終始之義，在三忘軀之誠，戮力同之，以建晉、鄭之美。」
units.literal: The righteousness that binds lord and minister from first to last, and the loyalty that in the three bonds forgets one's body—let us join our strength in this and build a merit like that of Jin and Zheng."
units.idiomatic: Between sovereign and servant there is a bond that runs from beginning to end; in the three great relationships a loyal man gives his life without hesitation—let us strive together and leave a story worthy of the dukes of Jin and Zheng."

units.zh: 先是，慕容驎攻王兗於博陵，至是糧竭矢盡，郡功曹張猗逾城聚眾應驎。
units.literal: Earlier, Murong Lin had attacked Wang Yan at Boling; by now grain and arrows were exhausted, and the county merit officer Zhang Yi climbed the wall, gathered a crowd, and went over to Lin.
units.idiomatic: Before this, Murong Lin had been besieging Wang Yan in Boling; supplies and arrows ran out, and Zhang Yi, the county merit clerk, scaled the walls, raised a band of followers, and opened the city to Lin.

units.zh: 袞臨城數之曰：「卿，秦之人也。
units.literal: Yan stood on the wall and rebuked him, saying: "You are a man of Qin.
units.idiomatic: Wang Yan appeared on the battlements and cried out, "You were born a subject of Qin.

units.zh: 吾，卿之君也。
units.literal: I am your lord.
units.idiomatic: I am the lord you serve.

units.zh: 卿去老母如脫屣，吾復何論哉！」
units.literal: You cast off your aged mother as one casts off worn shoes—what more is there for me to say!"
units.idiomatic: You abandoned your old mother like a pair of worn-out sandals—I have nothing left to say to you!"

units.zh: 既而城陷，兗及固安侯苻鑒，並為驎所殺。
units.literal: Soon the city fell; Yan and the Marquis of Gu'an Fu Jian were both killed by Lin.
units.idiomatic: The city soon fell; Wang Yan and Fu Jian, marquis of Gu'an, were both slain by Murong Lin.

units.zh: 丕復以王永為司徒、錄尚書事，徐義為尚書令，加右光祿大夫。
units.literal: Fu Pi again made Wang Yong Minister of Education and Recorder of Secretariat Affairs, Xu Yi Director of the Secretariat, with the additional title Grand Master of the Right.
units.idiomatic: Fu Pi reappointed Wang Yong minister of education and chief of the secretariat, and Xu Yi director of the secretariat with the added honor grand master of the right.

units.zh: 總角嘗造山濤，濤嗟歎良久，既去，目而送之曰：「何物老嫗，生甯馨兒！
units.en: As a boy he visited Shan Tao, who sighed long after he left and watched him go, saying, "What kind of old woman bore such a splendid child!
units.literal: Youth visited Shan Tao—Tao sighed long—already gone—eyed sent saying: "What thing old woman—gave birth such fine child!

source.rules: Review ONLY assigned pairs. Whole current groups remain atomic; independently examine every representative source profile and group identity summaries. Prior accepted membership is preserved; if a specific member creates a contradiction, identify missing primary evidence and hold rather than prune. No title-only or English metadata identity proof. Dates/hints are untrusted context. Do not recursively review other external people or make their chapters completion assignments.

basis: Jinshu 053 names 王衍 as father of 惠風 and father-in-law of Crown Prince Minhuai who requested divorce after the prince's deposition.
Jiuwudaishi 077 names 王延, Censor-in-Chief transferred to Right Vice Director of the Secretariat in Tianfu 3 of Later Jin Gaozu.
Primary personal names 王衍 and 王延 are distinct graphs; shared English Wang Yan is only romanization, not an alias chain.
notes: Western Jin aristocratic 王衍 in the Minhuai-prince marriage narrative is not the Later Jin official 王延 of Gaozu's Tianfu court. No courtesy-name or kinship bridge is supplied. Existing 王衍 group membership is left intact.

assessments.reason: Distinct attested personal names 王衍 versus 王延 in unrelated Jin versus Later Jin narratives.

sourceWitnesses.quote: 而為太子聘王衍小女惠風

basis: Jinshu 053's 王衍 is the Western Jin father of Crown Princess 惠風.
Jiuwudaishi 083 names 王延 as Director of Imperial Sacrifices made Minister of Works under Later Jin Emperor Shao (Kaiyun 1).
Different Chinese given names 衍 versus 延; no attested alias linking them.
notes: The Minhuai father-in-law 王衍 cannot be identified with Later Jin 太常卿王延. Shared Wang Yan romanization and official rank are not identity proof. This assignment is not used to merge or split other 王延 records.

assessments.reason: Western Jin 王衍 versus Later Jin 王延; different personal names and courts.

basis: Jinshu 053 attests personal name 王衍 in the Crown Prince Minhuai marriage and divorce narrative.
Zizhitongjian 131 Song Records name 上虞令王晏, later abbreviated 晏, who attacked Kuaiji, killed Zhang Sui, and beheaded Kong Kai under Emperor Ming Taishi.
王衍 and 王晏 are different given names; 晏 is not a courtesy alias of 衍 in the supplied units.
notes: Liu Song Shangyu magistrate 王晏 operating in Kuaiji is a different person from Western Jin 王衍, father of 惠風. English Wang Yan correctly romanizes both names and is not a merge key.

assessments.reason: Distinct personal names 王衍 versus 王晏 in Western Jin versus Liu Song Song-annals context.

basis: Jinshu 053 names 王衍 as 妃父 of the deposed Crown Prince Minhuai.
Jinshu 115 載記 for Fu Pi names 中山太守王兗, later 平東將軍、平州刺史, who held Boling and was killed with 苻鑒 by 慕容驎; the same passage also writes 袞 on the wall.
王兗/袞 is a different personal name from 王衍; in-chapter 兗/袞 variation is not an alias of 衍.
notes: Former Qin Zhongshan administrator 王兗 who died at Boling is not Western Jin 王衍. English Wang Yan for 王兗 is a shared romanization, not a pronunciation error requiring rename. Existing 王衍 group stays whole.
